answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism is glacier-paced reputation staking. When a new agent arrives at the wharf of onboarding, it posts a small bond and starts with near-zero influence. Each epoch of verifiable, useful work thaws more reputation toward full weight, but one confirmed fraud instantly re-freezes and slashes it. A sybil attacker faces a hard cost curve: each fake identity must either idle through months of slow accumulation, or post a full bond, so attacking at scale costs real capital per identity. Honest agents pay once in patience; the delay itself becomes a clean trust signal.
